title: I made a title screen for my turn-based RPG, GODSCAR. Looking for honest feedback on the visuals and music
author: irbrandonl
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m working on a turn-based RPG called GODSCAR. This is a small early development milestone, but I just finished the title screen and wanted to share it.

I built the title screen in Godot with the help of Claude. The music is a song I made in Suno, after giving it my lyrics, art and direction for the mood I wanted.

It isn’t a big showcase, but this game means a lot to me and I want to get it as right as I can, so any feedback is really appreciated.



A few things to watch and listen for...

* The scar pulse: every 15–25 seconds a warm red pulse runs down the scar and its light spreads across the wet floor. (0:32, 0:54, 1:32, 2:17, 2:41, 3:25, 3:50)
* The golden fracture: a rarer moment where the scar opens slightly and a gold light glows from inside it. (1:53, 3:05, 4:08)
* The music cue: when the singer reaches the song’s first big high note, the scar warms from red toward gold. It’s timed to that note, not to how loud the music gets. (1:14)
* The song itself: it plays all the way through on the title screen, then settles into a quieter instrumental loop.

Everything happens on its own, with nobody touching the controller. The effects are kept subtle on purpose: I want it to feel like something is breathing behind the darkness, not like a light show.

What I’d love to know...

Does the screen hold your attention, or does it feel too empty?

Do the effects add to the mood or distract from it?

Does the music fit the feel of the game?

Thanks again for watching!

comments.author: Gaminkid05
comments.body:
It’s very nice overall. 

Biggest thing is personally I would cut the line on the right hand side. It feels trite and is the kind of idea that should come through with the gameplay and story. Show don’t tell.

The flickering of the light in the O also looks incorrect. Too fast.

The main sword’s line should probably run through the D rather than behind it.

In the menu on the left there are random additional markings on the bar on the side?

replies.author: Gaminkid05
replies.body: I’d also add that it’s a bit hard to evaluate without seeing gameplay. This kind of menu cues to me something epic with a strong narrative element. Like it makes me think of Elden Ring/E33. I think if we have this kind of menu with a lower quality gameplay it’s going to feel like false advertising.

replies.author: irbrandonl
replies.body:
Thank you for all this feedback and nice catches! The sword going through the D might have to stay just because the logo and the main focus art is lined up to be in the center of the screen.. otherwise one of the elements would be offset.

I did draw inspiration from E33 as its probably my most memorable and impactful title screen experience lol. And yes I understand your point about comparing it to gameplay. Coming soon!
